name: Maysun bint Bahdal
bio: Maysun bint Bahdal (fl. c. 660) was a woman of the Banu Kalb, a Bedouin tribe of the Syrian desert. She married Mu'awiya, the future Umayyad caliph, while he was governor of Syria, and went with him to Damascus.

Tradition remembers her for a short poem in which she says she misses the tent, the simple wool cloak and the desert life she left behind, and prefers them to the palace; its last line is a scornful hit at her husband. Reynold A. Nicholson rendered it into English in 1922.

poems.title: A Tent with Rustling Breezes Cool
poems.author: Maysun bint Bahdal
poems.collection: Translations of Eastern Poetry and Prose (1922)
poems.text:
A tent with rustling breezes cool
Delights me more than palace high,
And more the cloak of simple wool
Than robes in which I learned to sigh.

The crust I ate beside my tent
Was more than this fine bread to me;
The wind's voice where the hill-path went
Was more than tambourine can be.

And more than purr of friendly cat
I love the watch-dog's bark to hear;
And more than any lubbard fat
I love a Bedouin cavalier!
